fields.ic_name: IEEE 1588 Precision Time Protocol (PTP) Clock Synchronization Engine (PTPv2 / IEEE 802.1AS)
fields.topology_type: Master-slave clock hierarchy over a packet network, rooted at the BMCA-elected Grandmaster. Ordinary Clocks are leaf/source nodes; Boundary Clocks terminate and regenerate PTP at boundaries; Transparent Clocks correct residence time in transit. The hierarchy spans a PTP domain over Ethernet or UDP.

supported_topologies.name: Grandmaster-rooted hierarchy
supported_topologies.description: The BMCA elects the Grandmaster; slaves discipline to it through a tree of Boundary / Transparent Clocks.

supported_topologies.name: Boundary Clock
supported_topologies.description: Multi-port; one SLAVE upstream, others MASTER downstream.

supported_topologies.name: Transparent Clock (P2P)
supported_topologies.description: Switch correcting residence time and measuring link delay (802.1AS).

master_slave_role_summary.description: BMCA-elected root and time reference for the domain.
Time source on a communication path; sends Sync / Announce.
Time receiver; sends Delay_Req and disciplines its clock.
Neither master nor slave on a path where another port is master.
Corrects residence time via the correctionField in transit.

fields.interconnect_role: PTP overlays a timing hierarchy on a packet network. The Grandmaster is the reference; Boundary Clocks segment the network and regenerate PTP; Transparent Clocks correct switching delay so accuracy is preserved across hops. Slaves compute offsetFromMaster and discipline their clocks.

ordering_guarantees.sync: A Sync (and its Follow_Up) precedes the corresponding Delay_Resp use; sequenceId orders messages.
ordering_guarantees.election: Announce collection -> BMCA decision -> port-state assignment.
ordering_guarantees.domain: Clocks in different domains do not interact.

fields.memory_vs_peripheral_regions: PTP is not memory-mapped; nodes are identified by clockIdentity (EUI-64) + portNumber and grouped by domainNumber. Configuration and status use PTP data sets via Management messages, not a memory or peripheral address.

device_classification.DTE: Data Terminal Equipment — endpoint host (PC, server, IP camera, IoT device).
device_classification.DCE: Data Circuit-terminating Equipment — switch port, router port, repeater port.
device_classification.PHY: Single-port PHY transceiver; one MII / GMII / RGMII data path + one MDI port + management bus interface.
device_classification.Multi-port_PHY: N MII / GMII ports on one chip with internal switch fabric.
device_classification.Switch_ASIC: Many ports + forwarding engine; one MAC + PHY pair per port; STA bus drives all PHYs.
device_classification.NIC: Network Interface Controller — MAC + PHY + DMA engine + host bus interface (PCIe).
device_classification.grandmaster: BMCA-elected root / time reference for the domain.
